t: A Bronze Age merchant state centred on Bahrain, linking Mesopotamia with the copper of Magan and the luxuries of the Indus.
Its springs, harbour, stamp seals and weight standard made it the clearing house of Gulf trade around 2000–1750 BCE.
Later ruled by Kassite governors and then a tributary of Assyria and Babylon, it vanished as a polity in the 6th century BCE.
dyk: Sumerian myth described Dilmun as a pure land without sickness or old age, where the gods settled the flood hero Ziusudra and gave him eternal life.
ev: Ur-Nanshe of Lagash records ships of Dilmun bringing him timber
Qal’at al-Bahrain becomes a walled town; temples rise at Barbar
Gulf trade contracts as the Indus cities decline and Babylon rises
Kassite Babylonia installs a governor on Bahrain
King Uperi of Dilmun sends gifts to Sargon II of Assyria
Dilmun passes with Babylonia to the Achaemenid Empire
Danish expedition under P.V. Glob and Geoffrey Bibby begins excavations
